spoken.said: This is a spoken cheat sheet on reading one Rust Rounds ticket on the phone, drawn from sample data. Reach for it when you want to see what a ticket asks, what was written in answer, and what the compiler said about it, all on one card. It is as of November twenty-first, twenty twenty-six, checked against some-ui.

spoken.narration: The card opens on the ticket: parse the batch without a copy per field. The spec says why it matters, a worker that misses its two millisecond target at peak. Below it, three points to speak to: where the time goes, what change removes it, and what that asks of the caller.

spoken.chapter: Chapter two. The program, and rustc's answer.
spoken.narration: Under the question sits the program written in answer. It copies the line into a new string, splits it, and returns pieces of that copy. rustc refuses it: the function returns a value that borrows a local it is about to drop. That error is the lesson the ticket was built to reach.
